name: client-2026-npc-dialog-self-close
summary: 2026 client: let the NPC quest dialog close itself on a button click again, as the 2016 client does, instead of waiting for a 0x442E no 2016 server sends.
status: UNTESTED in a live client as of 2026-09-17. Both edits validate against the original and the byte patterns are disassembled below; the behaviour is argued from the two binaries, not yet observed.
why: THE TARGET IS Fiesta.exe (2026-09-15, 9,264,128 B), NOT the Fiesta.bin beside it. That .bin is a stale
2026-08-19 build with no 0x442E handler and no 0x441F sender; the two are easy to confuse because both
contain 'quest_ack' and 'NpcDialogWin'.
WHAT THE TWO CLIENTS DO. A button in the quest speech bubble runs SpeechBubbleDlgWin::OnCommand, whose
common tail (2016 0x5FA38A) broadcasts window message 0x24 to the parent, NpcDialogWin::DirectMessage:
2016  0x5F5730:   if (keepOpen) keepOpen = 0;  else CloseWin(this);
2026  0x72B000:   if (keepOpen) keepOpen = 0;  if (g_C319D5 == 1) CloseWin(this);
So a 2016 client closes its quest dialog on EVERY click and lets the server's next QSC_SAY reopen it
(On_NC_QUEST_SCRIPT_CMD_REQ case 2 -> OpenNpcQuestDialog + ShowWin). keepOpen (+0x70 on the messenger
sub-object, +0x158 on the window) is set only by OpenNpcNormalDialog, never for a quest page.
2026 put a global in front of the close. g_C319D5 is cleared by OpenNpcQuestDialog (0x72A160) and
OpenUserQuestDialog (0x72AB80) on every page, and set by one quest packet only: 0x442E, handler
0x5B4BE0, which never reads its payload, sets the flag and calls NpcDialogWin close (0x72B1B0) on the
spot. A 2016 server has no such packet, so against one the flag is never 1 and the window never closes
by itself: Next and Complete Quest 'do nothing' on the last page of a script, Esc closes it (OnEscape
goes through CloseDialog, a different path), and the quest turns out to have progressed anyway.
THE PATCH restores the 2016 branch exactly, in three bytes:
0072B035  74 04  ->  74 0D      je   0x72B044        ; keepOpen clear -> straight to CloseWin
0072B03B  80 3D  ->  EB 25      jmp  0x72B062        ; keepOpen was set: consumed, skip the close
0072B03D  D5 19 C3 00 01 75 1E  (dead: the rest of the old cmp and its jne)
0072B044  ...                   CloseWin(this)
0x72B062 is the shared tail the old jne went to, so the fall-out path is the original one. There is a
base relocation at 0x72B03D (the flag's address operand). It is deliberately left in place: those four
bytes are now dead, so a rebase adjusts bytes nothing executes.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: remove the close-and-reopen between pages. That is native 2016 behaviour, not an
artefact - the 2016 client has always shut the window on a click and reopened it when the next SAY
arrived. The patch makes the close local and instant, which is how 2016 looks. Keeping the window up
between pages the way the official 2026 server does needs someone to know a page is the LAST one, and
only the server knows that.
The flag keeps its other reader (0x729E80) and all its writers, so the client still behaves normally
against a server that does send 0x442E: that handler closes the window itself.
ALTERNATIVE WITHOUT A CLIENT PATCH: fiesta-proxy Bridge2026 670816d sends 0x442E after every client
NC_QUEST_SCRIPT_CMD_ACK and swallows the ENDOFTRADE the 2026 close path emits. Same visible behaviour,
unmodified client. Use one or the other; with both, the bridge's 442E just closes an already-closed window.

edits.why: keepOpen clear: je straight to CloseWin (0x72B044) instead of to the g_C319D5 gate
keepOpen was set and is now consumed: jmp 0x72B062 over the close, replacing the gate's cmp
